rows.description: `lifeos.db` exists with WAL mode; `habit_log`, `lead_log`, `food_log`, `finance_transactions` tables present with correct typed columns; `tests/lifeos-db.test.ts` all green
rows.verifyMethod: `bun tests/lifeos-db.test.ts` exits 0; `sqlite3 lifeos.db "PRAGMA journal_mode"` → `wal`; `sqlite3 lifeos.db ".schema"` shows all four tables with expected columns

rows.description: `LifeOSQuery.ts` compiles under `tsc --strict --noEmit`; all typed accessors return correct types; write SQL strings are rejected (runtime guard or branded type)
rows.verifyMethod: `tsc --strict --noEmit` exits 0; test asserts that passing a non-SELECT SQL string to the Query API throws; return types verified by TypeScript narrowing in tests

rows.description: All Log rows backfilled from Workbook into `lifeos.db`; row counts match Sheets source-of-truth exactly (±0) per Log table
rows.verifyMethod: `bun bin/lifeos-migrate.ts && bun bin/lifeos-migrate-verify.ts` exits 0; no diff output; counts confirmed for `habit_log`, `lead_log`, `food_log`

rows.description: Router.ts Captures (Telegram + voice) land in `lifeos.db`; a test Capture sent via Telegram appears in `lifeos.db` within 5 seconds; Sheets write path is non-blocking
rows.verifyMethod: Send `/habit` via Telegram; `SELECT * FROM habit_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` returns the row within 5s; set `GOOGLE_SHEETS_URL=invalid` → send Capture → Router.ts returns success, row in `lifeos.db`, error in `logs/sheets-errors.log`

rows.description: Google OAuth consent screen status = "Published" in Google Cloud Console; Router.ts graceful-failure: Capture succeeds when Sheets is unreachable
rows.verifyMethod: Google Cloud Console → OAuth consent screen → Status shows "Published"; simulate Sheets unavailability → Router.ts logs soft error, Capture still lands in `lifeos.db`, no thrown exception

rows.description: `finance_transactions` populated from Plaid: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finance_transactions` > 0; `bin/plaid-sync.ts` exits 0; `PLAID_CLIENT_ID` present in `secrets.json`
rows.verifyMethod: `cat ~/.kaya/secrets.json | jq .PLAID_CLIENT_ID` non-empty; `bun bin/plaid-sync.ts` exits 0; `sqlite3 lifeos.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finance_transactions"` > 0

rows.description: Local web Dashboard at `localhost:PORT` renders four metric panels (habits, leads, finance, food) with real data from `lifeos.db`; each panel has working drill-down
rows.verifyMethod: `curl -s localhost:PORT/api/health` → `{"ok":true}`; open browser → all four panels show non-zero real data; clicking each panel shows last 14 days of Log rows

rows.description: Jm can run `kaya lifeos audit lead`, locate a specific lead by name, read its last 3 Log entries, identify any anomalies — all within 5 minutes
rows.verifyMethod: Jm live-demos: runs audit command, locates named lead, reads 3 entries, completes inspection; wall-clock time < 5 minutes

rows.description: 08:00 daily briefing fires and contains habit summary sourced from `lifeos.db` (via Query API); confirmed in launchd logs
rows.verifyMethod: Manually trigger: `launchctl start com.kaya.briefing`; check `logs/briefing-$(date +%Y%m%d).log` → contains habit summary with today's date; `log show --predicate 'process contains "briefing"' --last 1h` shows run

rows.description: All 13 launchd jobs loaded and non-error; `launchctl list | grep com.kaya | wc -l` = 13; no job shows repeated non-zero last-exit
rows.verifyMethod: `launchctl list | grep com.kaya | wc -l` = 13; no entry in `launchctl list` output has repeated non-zero `LastExitStatus`; `bin/rebuild-plists.sh` runs clean
